editorial.marketOverview: Friday's US closing data remain the latest observable cash-market state. Reuters reports Nasdaq Composite down 5.28% and semiconductor index down roughly 11%, while a secondary source reports QQQ down 5.67%. AP's November 21 recap confirms Nasdaq -5.3%, S&P 500 -3.7% and a roughly 10% weekly Nasdaq decline. Barron's Friday VIX close was 37.66. These observations support persistent elevated downside risk, not a new Saturday price signal.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the preceding 06:28 EST snapshot, a fresh review of Reuters' November 20 close and AP's November 21 index recap adds corroboration but no independently verified path-changing catalyst. The curated Open Watch file remains 174 events with update timestamp 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00. No new US cash session has occurred. Bias, confidence and event risk remain unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor leadership deteriorated more severely than the broad Nasdaq, and extreme Friday volatility and negative breadth favor caution. The same positioning stress creates conditions for a violent short-covering rebound; that would not by itself confirm a durable turn. The older 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% imply a +29 basis point curve, but those are stale and should not be paired with a later 10Y reading. Direct synchronized Fed probabilities, VXN, oil contracts and breadth were not established. Headlines' prospective impact is not proof of a causally observed market reaction.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: elevated gap and liquidation risk versus oversold relief, with 09:45 ET flash PMIs testing macro expectations. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Analog Devices/Dell earnings may test demand and chip sentiment. Wednesday November 25: GDP, PCE/personal spending, durable goods and Beige Book present high repricing risk. These are scheduled catalysts, not observed outcomes; a sustained positive path requires confirmation in semiconductor participation, breadth and volatility.
editorial.bullCase: A deeply oversold Nasdaq and elevated Friday VIX can fuel short covering; a sustained bull case requires QQQ, SOX and SMH recovering in tandem, improving breadth and falling VIX/VXN. Lower Treasury yields could support duration-sensitive technology only if verified with comparable timestamped rates.
editorial.bearCase: Nasdaq's roughly 10% weekly loss, severe SOX underperformance and a VIX close above 37 make failed rallies and further deleveraging plausible. Hawkish inflation surprises or weak AI hardware guidance would amplify pressure if they occur; they have not yet occurred.
editorial.watchNext: At Monday reopening verify synchronized QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX/SMH, VIX/VXN and breadth; independently confirm both Treasury maturities and FedWatch, plus contract-matched Brent and WTI. Track flash PMIs Monday, consumer confidence and ADI/Dell Tuesday, Wednesday's macro slate and Beige Book. Compare any new Open Watch entries before labeling a catalyst as market-confirmed.
